chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Muthanna, from Zurara ibn A'yan and Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Udaym the seller of Al-Harawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

The Mu'allaqah (woman subjected to li'an), if her husband curses her, she does not become permissible for him ever; and the one who marries the woman during her waiting period while he knows, she does not become permissible for him ever; and the one who divores with the divorce of 'Iddah which is not permissible for him until she marries another husband, having divorced her three times and married her three times, she does not become permissible for him ever; and the Muhrim (one in consecration for Hajj or Umrah), when he marries while he knows that it is prohibited upon him, she does not become permissible for him ever.

key_terms.الطَّلَاقَ الثَّلَاثَ: Triple divorce, where three divorces are pronounced, requiring a subsequent marriage to another man before remarriage to the first.
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (consecration) for Hajj or Umrah.
key_terms.الْمُلَاعَنَةُ: Li'an, the mutual cursing between husband and wife to prove/disprove paternity or fidelity, resulting in permanent prohibition.
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: Her waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death, during which she cannot remarry.
key_terms.لَمْ تَحِلَّ لَهُ أَبَداً: She does not become permissible for him ever (permanent prohibition).

ai.seo_question: What are the four cases where a woman becomes permanently prohibited to her husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'Dahr' (permanent prohibition) for four specific scenarios, emphasizing that the barrier is absolute and not merely temporary. It highlights the juristic consensus on the finality of Li'an, the validity of marriage during 'Iddah, the mechanics of Triple Talaq requiring a subsequent marriage, and the status of the Muhrim, reflecting key Shia fiqh rulings on marital impediments.
